correctness.rationale: For an orthotope, Cauchy projection brightness equals sum_i a_i |v_i|. Averaging normal v uniformly in u^perp yields c_d sum_i a_i sqrt(1−u_i²), exactly the probability-normalized Radon operator, a Minkowski sum of coordinate-hyperplane disks. With t_i=u_i², support f(t)=sum_i a_i sqrt(1−t_i) is strictly concave on the simplex; min at a vertex gives inradius c_d(S−A). KKT and complementary slackness yield a unique multiplier λ via sum(1−a_i²/λ²)_+=1 and unique squared maximizing normal, hence exhaustive active-set circumradius. Evaluating the diagonal normal and A/S≥1/d yields the sharp R/r≥sqrt(d/(d−1)) with equality only when all a_i, equivalently all side lengths, coincide. The d3 active-set partition yields both square-root/linear branches, with second derivative discontinuity. Independent 600 sampled positive-weight tests in dimensions 3,4,6,9 verified KKT, support values, the sharp ratio and all 3D phase boundaries, but finite tests are not the proof.
